16084473.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection / surveillance from radiology reports
16084473.patient_population: neonates (newborns) whose radiology reports were screened for healthcare-associated pneumonia
16084473.model_description: An NLP-based automated monitoring system reads free-text radiology reports and classifies them for presence of pneumonia, to support surveillance of healthcare-associated pneumonia in newborns. Its output was compared against clinicians' judgments in a feasibility study; the abstract does not describe the underlying training method or imaging modality in detail.

17242901.model_family: back-propagation / radial basis function / support vector machine neural networks with fuzzy logic
17242901.patient_population: children from infancy through adolescence undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment
17242901.model_description: The system automatically segments phalanx and carpal regions on hand radiographs and extracts geometric and morphological features. Back-propagation, radial basis function, and support vector machine neural networks classify phalanx bone age, combined with a fuzzy assessment based on the normalized carpal bone area ratio, to extend automated bone age assessment to younger children where carpal features are more informative than phalanx features alone.
17242901.study_design: technical development and retrospective algorithm validation

17369018.model_family: knowledge-based automatic segmentation with fuzzy classification (computer-aided diagnosis)
17369018.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in young children
17369018.patient_population: children from newborn to 7 years old, hand radiographs from a digital hand atlas
17369018.model_description: Building on an existing phalanx-based CAD bone-age system that worked well only from age 7 onward, this method automatically segments carpal bone boundaries on hand radiographs, extracts morphological features, and applies fuzzy classification to estimate bone age. It was evaluated on about 205 cases from a digital hand atlas against chronological age and two radiologists' readings.
17369018.dataset_size: about 205 cases from a digital hand atlas
17369018.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation against radiologist readings

18440892.clinical_problem: skeletal age estimation using the Tanner-Whitehouse (TW3) method
18440892.patient_population: children undergoing hand/wrist radiography for skeletal age assessment (private hand image database)
18440892.model_description: The system automates the Tanner-Whitehouse (TW3) skeletal-age method by semi-automatically segmenting the radius and ulna on hand radiographs, extracting up to 89 shape and grayscale features, and classifying bone maturity stages with a Generalized Softmax Perceptron neural network. Stage predictions are combined via the TW3 methodology to output a bone age in years, evaluated against pediatrician and radiologist expert readings on a private hand image database.
18440892.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation against expert readings

21995007.model_family: voxelwise multivariate regression / log-Euclidean full-diffusion-tensor machine learning framework
21995007.clinical_problem: predicting a clinical severity score from brain diffusion MRI in autism spectrum disorder
21995007.patient_population: 30 children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder
21995007.model_description: The method performs brain-wide prediction of a clinical score directly from the full diffusion tensor at each voxel, using a log-Euclidean framework rather than reducing each tensor to fractional anisotropy alone. Full-tensor information is carried through registration, smoothing, and multivariate voxelwise feature selection before score prediction. Tested on diffusion MRI from 30 children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder, it showed some improvement over an FA-only analysis.

23554109.clinical_problem: identifying pneumonia from chest radiograph reports
23554109.patient_population: mixed pediatric and adult patients (from infants to elderly adults) with chest radiograph reports, used for pneumonia outcome validation
23554109.model_description: ONYX is an NLP system trained on previously manually reviewed chest radiograph reports from both children and adults. It classifies each report as consistent with pneumonia, inconsistent with pneumonia, or requiring manual review, and can be tuned either to optimize accuracy or to minimize the amount of manual review needed. Sensitivity and specificity were further modeled by patient age, comorbidity, and care setting using logistic regression.
23554109.headline_result: Accuracy-tailored setting: sensitivity 92% (95% CI 90-93%), specificity 87% (86-88%), PPV 74%, NPV 96%; review-minimizing setting: sensitivity 75%, specificity 95%, PPV 86%, NPV 91%

24936426.clinical_problem: classifying childhood epilepsy activity/intractability from diffusion tensor imaging
24936426.patient_population: 49 participants including 20 children with epilepsy (5-6 years after seizure onset, grouped as active vs. remitted) and healthy controls
24936426.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging metrics (fractional anisotropy, mean diffusivity, radial and axial diffusivity) from children with epilepsy and healthy controls were used to train a support vector machine classifier (10-fold cross-validation) that automatically distinguishes controls from children with epilepsy, and separately distinguishes active from remitted epilepsy. Mean diffusivity gave the best two-way classification and fractional anisotropy the best three-way classification.
24936426.dataset_size: 49 participants (20 children with epilepsy plus healthy controls)
24936426.headline_result: SVM with mean diffusivity: sensitivity 90-100%, specificity 96.6-100% (controls vs. all epilepsy); SVM with fractional anisotropy: 100% sensitivity and specificity for the three-way classification (controls vs. active vs. remitted epilepsy)
24936426.study_design: case-control diagnostic imaging study with SVM classification

26850738.model_family: random forest classifier on structural (diffusion MRI) connectome and demographic features
26850738.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive impairment in survivors of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia from brain structural connectivity
26850738.patient_population: 31 survivors of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ages 5-19) treated with chemotherapy only, compared with 39 matched healthy controls
26850738.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging was used to build whole-brain structural connectomes, analyzed with graph-theoretical measures (small-worldness, clustering coefficient) in young survivors of acute lymphoblastic leukemia versus healthy controls. A random forest model combining connectome and demographic variables was then trained to automatically classify survivors as having cognitive impairment or not.

26850738.headline_result: Random forest classification accuracy 0.89 (p < 0.0001) for cognitive impairment status
26850738.study_design: case-control diagnostic imaging study with random forest classification

26900607.clinical_problem: identifying infants at high risk for autism spectrum disorder from diffusion MRI connectomes
26900607.patient_population: infants at 6 months of age at high familial risk for autism spectrum disorder
26900607.model_description: A multi-kernel support vector machine framework combines diffusion parameters from a hierarchical set of white-matter connectomes, derived from diffusion MRI, to identify 6-month-old infants at high risk for autism spectrum disorder before behavioral signs emerge. Combining information across the hierarchical connectomes improved classification accuracy over using the single best connectome alone.
26900607.headline_result: Classification accuracy of 76%, versus 70% with the best single connectome
26900607.study_design: case-control diagnostic imaging study, machine learning classification (workshop paper)
